about: Easton's entries left out of the app because they teach against the King James Bible with the Apocrypha or the IUIC classes (owner's direction, 2026-10-26 and 2026-11-02). The reasons and the verses or classes are in the doctrine audit.

terms.why: Says the first day of the week is now the Sabbath (Exodus 20:10; 31:16).
Reads Revelation 1:10 as the first day of the week.
Teaches the Trinity, which the classes reject.
"The third Person of the adorable Trinity."
Teaches the Trinity and a sonship of equality, against the classes.
Reads today's Jews as Israel (Revelation 2:9; 3:9).
Church doctrine of the old and new dispensations and infant membership.
Says the covenant "is abrogated under the gospel".
Says the law was abrogated ("the abrogation of the Mosaic institutes").
Reads the law as bondage and Sarah as "the Christian church".
Calls Joseph "The foster-father of our Lord"; the classes teach Joseph is the father of Christ and of his brethren (Matthew 13:55; Luke 4:22; John 6:42).
Says the brethren of Jesus may be cousins, sons of Joseph "by a former marriage" or children of "the Virgin's sister" (Matthew 13:55-56).
Calls James "the brother" or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord" (Galatians 1:19; Matthew 13:55).
Calls her the "Virgin Mary" and says Joseph "was supernaturally made aware": virgin-birth framing.
Reads Isaiah 7:14 as "a prophecy concerning our Lord": virgin-birth framing.
"Most Christian interpreters have regarded these words as ... a prophecy of our Saviour": virgin-birth framing.
Calls Christ "the virgin's son (Isa. 7:14)".
"Christ is both God and man ... The union is hypostatical": Jesus as God.
"This title designates the divine nature of Christ": Jesus as God.
"Such a mediator must be at once divine and human": Jesus as God.
"the Son of God, in whom deity and humanity become one": Jesus as God.
"his person as God-man": Jesus as God.
"his act of becoming incarnate": Jesus as God.
"foreshadowings of the incarnation": Jesus as God.
Attributes creation "to the Godhead ... to the Father ... to the Son ... to the Holy Spirit": the Trinity.
"the whole nature and attributes of God are in Christ"; "the church as the fulness".
"the true humanity of our Lord": the two-natures doctrine.
"the rational, immortal soul" and "the divine nature".
"the invisible catholic church": the church in place of Israel.
Takes the subjects of the kingdom to be "the Church".
"used sometimes to denote the Church of God": the church in place of Israel.
"a type of the gospel Church": the church in place of Israel.
Reads the loaves as "the entire spiritual Israel, 'the true Israel;'": the church in place of Israel.
"The church is the 'property' of God": the church in place of Israel (Deuteronomy 14:2).
"The Jewish eldership was transferred from the old dispensation to the new".
The relation "of the Jewish to the Christian dispensation".
Applies the tithe to "the Christian Church"; the classes teach it belonged to the Levites (Numbers 18:21).
The ceremonial law "was obligatory only till Christ": the law done away.
"the old covenant of works, which is superseded": the law done away.
"a temporary economy ... have now passed away": the law done away.
"the abrogation of the Levitical system": the law done away.
"a sign and seal of the covenant of grace"; "Under the Jewish dispensation, church and state were identical".
Covenant theology the classes do not teach.
Vicarious substitution doctrine of the churches.
"vicarious satisfaction" doctrine of the churches.
"the vicarious punishment which he endured": church doctrine.
Imputed-righteousness doctrine of the churches.
"the sin of Adam is imputed to all his descendants": church doctrine.
Original sin and "the covenant of works": church doctrine.
"Original sin" imputed to all: church doctrine.
Church doctrine of adoption by justification.
Calvinist election doctrine.
Calvinist predestination doctrine.
Calvinist doctrine ("the covenant of grace").
Calvinist doctrine of the decrees.
Church regeneration doctrine.
Church sanctification doctrine.
Defines faith by "the Assembly's Shorter Catechism".
"the Word, Sacraments, and Prayer": church sacraments.
"a satisfaction to divine justice ... a ransom from the curse and authority of the law".
"a permanent ordinance in the Church of Christ"; "eucharist", "mass".
The Lord's Supper as a church ordinance.
"The sacramental cup".
